description: Browser automation CLI for AI agents

latest_release.name: v0.41.2
latest_release.body:
### New Features

- Added **targeted skill references** with `skills get <name> --ref <ref>` and the MCP `agent_browser_skills_get` tool's `refs` argument, so agents can load one reference or template at a time (#2310)
- Added **Chrome security warnings** when newer stable releases list CVE fixes, without blocking commands. Set `AGENT_BROWSER_NO_VERSION_CHECK=1` to skip the check (#2309)

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed **session restarts** when commands omit or change timeout settings, preserving open pages and reusing the running daemon's default timeout for waits (#2288)
- Fixed **bare `open`** dropping configured profiles and browser arguments and relaunching Chrome with a temporary profile (#2287)
- Fixed **browserless commands** starting a browser when launch options are set in the environment (#2309)
- Fixed **Windows home directory detection** to respect `USERPROFILE`, and kept the MCP tool catalog's line endings consistent for Windows tests (#2305)

### Improvements

- Slimmed **the core agent skill** and routed detailed guidance to references, with instructions to pass `--session` on every command (#2303, #2312)

### Documentation

- Simplified **the README**, moved detailed guidance to the docs site, and corrected source build instructions (#2302)

### Contributors

detail.readme_excerpt:
# agent-browser Browser automation for AI agents: open pages, read them as an accessibility tree, and act on elements from the shell.

agent-browser is a native Rust CLI that gives an AI agent a browser it can drive one command at a time. `snapshot` returns the page as compact text with a ref such as `@e1` for each element. The agent acts on a ref, reads the page again to check the result, and repeats. The browser stays open between commands, so each step is one short shell call. ## Install ```bash npm install -g agent-browser agent-browser install # download Chrome for Testing (first time only) ``` - **Homebrew:** `brew install agent-browser`, then `agent-browser install`. - **Linux:** `agent-browser install --with-deps` also installs the browser's system libraries. - **No install:** `npx agent-browser open example.com`. Project installs, building from source, `upgrade`, and `doctor` are covered in [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/installation). ## Quick start ```bash agent-browser open example.com agent-browser snapshot -i # interactive elements, each with a ref agent-browser click @e1 # act on a ref from that snapshot agent-browser get url # check the result agent-browser close ``` The snapshot for `example.com`: ``` - link "Learn more" [ref=e1] ``` - Refs describe the page at the time of the snapshot. After navigation or a DOM change, take a new snapshot before using refs again. - CSS selectors, text, XPath, and semantic locators also work, for example `agent-browser find role button click --name "Submit"`. See [Selectors](https://agent-browser.dev/selectors). - A click fails, instead of reporting success, when the target is hidden, disabled, outside the viewport, or covered by another element such as a consent banner.
